areas.area: OmniStudio (Omnistudio) — OmniScript, FlexCard, Data Mapper/DataRaptor, Integration Procedure, Business Rules Engine, DataPack/CLI deployment, caching + governor interaction, runtime/licensing model

practices.practice: Treat Setup > Omnistudio Settings > 'Managed Package Runtime' = Off as a one-way door: verify every business-critical FlexCard and OmniScript on standard objects first, and confirm CME/ISV component certification, before flipping it.
practices.specifics: Setup > Omnistudio Settings > Managed Package Runtime. Doc text: "After you disable the managed package runtime setting, you shouldn't re-enable it." After disabling, changes made to OmniScripts/FlexCards do NOT automatically flow to custom components already deployed in Lightning App Builder pages and communities — you must re-run 'Deploy Custom Lightning Web Components in Standard Runtime' (minutes to ~1 hour; watch Setup > Deployment Status).
practices.why_it_matters: This is the single largest architectural switch in OmniStudio and there is no supported rollback path. Getting it wrong strands every deployed custom LWC on a stale definition.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs describe the managed-package→standard-runtime switch as a reversible toggle ('just turn it back on if something breaks') and skip the pre-flight entirely. They also conflate 'Managed Package Runtime' with 'Managed Package Designer' — the Designer toggle IS reversible (Setup > Omnistudio Settings > Managed Package Designer back to On), the Runtime one is not.
practices.gating_licence_or_permission: Requires the Omnistudio permission set license enabled in the org before standard runtime content will run.

practices.practice: Before enabling standard Omnistudio runtime, explicitly set FLS on three objects for every profile that will run OmniStudio, or components fail after cutover.
practices.specifics: Field-level security must be explicitly set for: Omni Process Compilation (Read, Edit), Omni Data Transformation (Read), Omniscript Saved Sessions (Read, Edit). Standard runtime "enforces field-level security (FLS) more strictly" than the managed-package runtime, so permissions that were implicitly tolerated before become hard failures.
practices.why_it_matters: This is the most common post-cutover breakage: the OmniScript renders for the admin (who has everything) and dies for the end-user profile.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: An LLM asked 'what permissions do users need for OmniStudio?' answers with the generic 'assign the OmniStudio User permission set' and never names Omni Process Compilation / Omni Data Transformation / Omniscript Saved Sessions. Those three objects are the actual gate in standard runtime.
practices.gating_licence_or_permission: FLS Read+Edit on Omni Process Compilation; Read on Omni Data Transformation; Read+Edit on Omniscript Saved Sessions — per profile.

practices.practice: Size the Omnistudio licence by persona: the designer add-on and the runtime add-on are separate SKUs mapping to two different permission sets under one permission set licence.
practices.specifics: Permission set licence: 'Omnistudio'. SKU OmnistudioDesignerAddOn → persona 'Omnistudio Admin' → permission set 'Omnistudio Admin' → create OmniScripts, Data Mappers, FlexCards, Integration Procedures (includes calculation runtime). SKU OmnistudioRuntimeAddOn → persona 'Omnistudio User' → permission set 'Omnistudio User' → execute only. Document Generation is a separate PSL stack: DocGenPlus (PSL 'DocGen Designer', permission sets DocGen Designer + DocGen User, 10,000 Designer PSLs); DocGenDesigner is End of Sale; DocGenRuntimeCC (PSL 'DocGen Runtime for Community Users') is what Experience Cloud site users need to generate documents, and becomes optional for new customers from Winter '26.
practices.why_it_matters: Buying only the runtime add-on means nobody in the org can author; buying only designer means end users cannot execute. Experience Cloud DocGen is a distinct purchase entirely.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs say 'OmniStudio is included with Industry Clouds' and stop. They do not distinguish OmnistudioDesignerAddOn from OmnistudioRuntimeAddOn, and they never mention that Experience Cloud document generation needs the separate DocGenRuntimeCC / 'DocGen Runtime for Community Users' PSL — so community users hit a hard block at go-live.
practices.gating_licence_or_permission: Omnistudio permission set licence + Omnistudio Admin (design) or Omnistudio User (runtime) permission set; DocGen Runtime for Community Users PSL for Experience Cloud DocGen.

practices.practice: Assign Business Rules Engine access by permission set licence, not by profile: Rule Engine Runtime for executors, Rule Engine Designer for authors, plus Context Service and Decision Explainer sets when used.
practices.specifics: Rule Engine Runtime PSL = run expression sets and lookup tables, Read on BRE objects, read decision tables. Rule Engine Designer PSL = all of that plus Create/Update/Delete on BRE objects and decision tables, and use of context definition tags as list variables. Additional permission sets: Context Service Admin (create/activate context definitions), Context Service Runtime (execute expression sets that use context tags as list variables), Decision Explainer Service Access (step explanations and action logging for expression set executions).
practices.why_it_matters: An expression set that works for the architect fails for the service agent purely on PSL assignment, and the failure surfaces as an empty/null result rather than an access error.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs invent names like 'Business Rules Engine User' or 'BRE Admin'. The real names are Rule Engine Runtime and Rule Engine Designer, and the Context Service pair is a separate requirement most answers omit entirely — so list-variable expression sets fail at runtime for everyone but the admin.
practices.gating_licence_or_permission: Rule Engine Runtime / Rule Engine Designer permission set licences; Context Service Admin / Context Service Runtime; Decision Explainer Service Access.

practices.practice: Design expression sets against the published per-version ceilings, not against 'it compiles' — the step and business-element ceilings are low enough that a single monolithic pricing rule will hit them.
practices.specifics: Expression Set default limits per version: 200 steps, 50 business elements, 1,000 local resources, 5 object aliases, 100 object field aliases, 100 context tags usable as list variables, 200 conditions per conditional group, subexpression depth 2 levels, 5,000,000 executions per hour. Decision Matrix: 100 MB max CSV, 200 simultaneous input set lookups, 400,000 invocations per hour.
practices.why_it_matters: Subexpression depth of 2 is the one that bites: deeply nested calculation logic must be decomposed into separate expression sets, which changes the whole decomposition strategy up front.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs happily design a 400-step expression set with 4 levels of nested subexpressions because nothing in their training says otherwise. The 200-step / depth-2 pair is the actual design constraint and is never mentioned.

practices.practice: Pick standard vs advanced decision tables from the row and column ceilings, because the gap between them is two orders of magnitude and migrating later means re-authoring.
practices.specifics: Standard decision tables: 100,000 processable rows, 15 table columns, 30 input conditions, 10 output results per lookup, 20 simultaneously active tables, 200 row groups × 25,000 rows per group, 50 output rows returned for a single lookup / 200 for multiple, 40 full refreshes per hour, 2,000,000 invocations/hour. Advanced decision tables: 20,000,000 processable rows, 100 simultaneously active tables, 31 matched columns, 10 unmatched columns, 10 output columns, 200 rows per AND-column combination, 40,000 output rows for multiple lookups, incremental refresh up to 1,000,000 rows, 60 full refreshes/hour, 5 referenced objects, 10,800,000 invocations/hour. CSV-based decision tables: 1,000,000 processable rows but only 50,000 uploadable rows, 5 simultaneous uploads, 5 simultaneous downloads.
practices.why_it_matters: The CSV asymmetry (1,000,000 processable vs 50,000 uploadable) silently caps a bulk rate-table load; teams discover it mid-migration.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs treat 'decision table' as one thing and quote no numbers. They never surface the standard/advanced/CSV split, and never warn that a CSV rate table above 50,000 rows cannot be uploaded even though the engine can process 1,000,000.

practices.practice: When an Integration Procedure will exceed a synchronous transaction, set Chainable (or Queueable Chainable) and tune the per-chain governor thresholds explicitly — the defaults are the platform synchronous limits, and Queueable Chainable is what raises them.
practices.specifics: Chainable configuration defaults: Queries 100, DML statements 150, CPU 10,000 ms, heap 6 MB, DML rows 10,000, query rows 50,000, SOSL queries 20, plus a configurable 'Actual Time' seconds threshold. Queueable Chainable overrides: heap 12 MB, CPU 60,000 ms, queries 200. Maximum stack depth for chained jobs is 5 (i.e. you can chain four times after the parent). Enable via the Chainable checkbox on the Integration Procedure Action, the Queueable checkbox, chainable=true / queueableChainable=true in REST calls, or Chain On Step on an individual long-running step.
practices.why_it_matters: 6 MB → 12 MB heap and 10,000 ms → 60,000 ms CPU is the difference between a working and a failing bulk IP, and it is a checkbox, not a redesign.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs advise 'move it to Batch Apex' the moment an IP is slow, missing Queueable Chainable entirely. They also state or imply that chainable settings are just advisory tuning knobs rather than the actual per-chain governor budget, and never mention the depth-5 chain ceiling.

practices.practice: Never architect an Apex class to call a chainable Integration Procedure — chainable IPs are only invocable from REST API, an OmniScript, or a parent Integration Procedure.
practices.specifics: Documented constraint: chainable Integration Procedures cannot be called directly from Apex classes. Non-chainable IPs can be invoked from Apex (see 'Integration Procedure Invocation from Apex'), from Flow, and from REST.
practices.why_it_matters: Teams design an Apex service layer that wraps a chainable IP, then discover at integration-test time that the entry point is unusable and the whole call chain has to be inverted.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: An LLM will confidently emit Apex sample code calling a chainable IP through the IP invocation API, because non-chainable invocation from Apex IS documented and it does not distinguish the two.

practices.practice: For long-running external callouts, use Omnistudio.OmniContinuation — VlocityContinuationIntegration is the deprecated predecessor kept only for backward compatibility. Enable it with 'Use Continuation' on the IP Action, or with an Options Map on a FlexCard data source.
practices.specifics: Class: Omnistudio.OmniContinuation (namespace-independent, recommended). Deprecated: VlocityContinuationIntegration. OmniScript → long-running IP: check the 'Use Continuation' setting on the Integration Procedure Action. FlexCard → long-running IP with HTTP or Remote Action: add an Options Map to the data source with key useContinuation and value true.
practices.why_it_matters: The FlexCard path is an Options Map key, not a checkbox — there is no UI toggle, so it is simply never configured unless you know the key name.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs still recommend VlocityContinuationIntegration (it dominates older blog content) and, for FlexCards, invent a non-existent 'Use Continuation' checkbox instead of the useContinuation Options Map key.

practices.practice: When enabling top-level Integration Procedure caching, assert on the returned cache telemetry nodes and keep user-scoped data out of org-level cache.
practices.specifics: Procedure Configuration properties: 'Salesforce Platform Cache Type' (session or org) and 'Time To Live In Minutes'. Response nodes emitted when caching is active: vlcCacheKey (the cache key), vlcCacheResult (true when served from cache), vlcCacheEnabled (false when ignoreCache disabled it), vlcCacheException (caching errors). Preview settings: ignoreCache default true (does not clear or save to cache), resetCache default false (forces a save). A failing IP is not cached. Clear cache via Connect APIs for session, org, or all levels, keyed on IP key + input parameters.
practices.why_it_matters: vlcCacheResult is the only reliable way to prove a cache is actually being hit; without it teams 'enable caching' and measure no improvement because ignoreCache defaults to true in preview.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs describe OmniStudio caching in generic Platform Cache terms and never name vlcCacheKey / vlcCacheResult / vlcCacheEnabled / vlcCacheException, so the guidance is untestable. They also miss that ignoreCache defaults to true in Preview, which makes cache testing in the designer misleading.

practices.practice: Choose Org Cache vs Session Cache from the hard TTL ceilings and the data sensitivity, and allocate the VlocityMetadata Platform Cache partition if you rely on Scale Cache metadata caching.
practices.specifics: Org Cache: shared across all users in the org, maximum TTL 48 hours, intended for non-sensitive data such as picklists and configuration. Session Cache: user-scoped, tied to the active session, maximum TTL 8 hours. Automatic metadata caching happens via Scale Cache unless turned off; if you use Platform Cache you must allocate space in the VlocityMetadata cache partition to enable that automatic caching.
practices.why_it_matters: Putting record-scoped or FLS-sensitive data in Org Cache leaks it to every user in the org; the 8-hour session ceiling is what forces reference data into org scope.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs give TTL advice in minutes with no ceiling ('set it to a day or two'), unaware that Session Cache caps at 8 hours and Org Cache at 48. They also never name the VlocityMetadata partition, so the allocation step that makes metadata caching work is missing.
practices.gating_licence_or_permission: Platform Cache allocation on the VlocityMetadata partition.

practices.practice: Know that FlexCards are cached by default and that the switch lives on Omni Interaction Access Configuration, not on the card.
practices.specifics: Setting name: 'Disable Card Cache', default unchecked (caching ON). Configured on Omni Interaction Access Configuration records at org level (the 'Org_Wide' record), by profile, or by user — available since Winter '22. What is cached: FlexCards, custom labels, and profile data, loaded from the VlocityMetadata partition of Platform Cache. Companion settings on the same object: 'Enable Async Card Caching' (runs card caching via Future method calls) and a user-information caching toggle.
practices.why_it_matters: 'I published the FlexCard but users still see the old one' is almost always this setting, and the fix is on a config object most admins have never opened.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs debug stale FlexCards by telling you to clear browser cache, re-activate the card, or check the Lightning page assignment. The actual lever — 'Disable Card Cache' on the Org_Wide Omni Interaction Access Configuration record — is never named.
practices.gating_licence_or_permission: Access to Setup > Omni Interaction Access Configuration.

practices.practice: Audit Required Permission on every Data Mapper and Integration Procedure: a blank Required Permission with no DefaultRequiredPermission means any authenticated user can execute it.
practices.specifics: Omnistudio security settings: DefaultRequiredPermission (org-wide baseline; if unset and the component's Required Permission is blank, any user can run it), CheckCachedMetadataRecordSecurity (default False — when False, cached metadata bypasses record-level security checks that Sharing Settings/Sharing Sets would otherwise apply), EnforceDMFLSAndDataEncryption (enforces field-level security across all Data Mappers when enabled). Doc text: "If Required Permission is blank, any user can run the Data Mapper or Integration Procedure unless the DefaultRequiredPermission property is set."
practices.why_it_matters: This is the highest-severity default in OmniStudio: a guest-accessible Experience Cloud page plus an unrestricted Data Mapper is an unauthenticated data read, and it fails open silently with no error anywhere.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: Asked to secure OmniStudio, an LLM answers with 'use with sharing', 'enforce FLS in Apex', and permission sets — the generic Salesforce answer. It does not know that OmniStudio components default to open execution and that DefaultRequiredPermission / EnforceDMFLSAndDataEncryption / CheckCachedMetadataRecordSecurity are the actual named controls.
practices.gating_licence_or_permission: DefaultRequiredPermission org setting; per-component Required Permission (profile, role, or custom permission); EnforceDMFLSAndDataEncryption.

practices.practice: Turn on OmniStudio error logging deliberately — it is off until you create the config record, and the log tab is hidden until you switch it on per profile.
practices.specifics: Create an Omni Interaction Configuration setting with Label ErrorLoggingEnabled, Name ErrorLoggingEnabled (no spaces, case preserved), Value true. Errors then land as OmniComponentErrorLog sObject records: error detail and response in the Input field, the message in the ErrorMessage field. To view them, set the 'Omni Component Error Logs' tab to Default On in Tab Settings on the relevant profiles, then open the Omni Component Error Logs app from App Launcher.
practices.why_it_matters: Without this, production Integration Procedure failures leave no server-side trace at all — you are reduced to reproducing in Preview.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs point at debug logs, the OmniScript 'Debug' panel, or a fictional 'OmniStudio Error Log' object. The exact record name ErrorLoggingEnabled (case-sensitive, no spaces) and the sObject OmniComponentErrorLog with its Input/ErrorMessage fields are not in their answer, so the reader enables nothing.
practices.gating_licence_or_permission: 'Omni Component Error Logs' tab set to Default On in profile Tab Settings.

practices.practice: An Integration Procedure step that errors does not stop the procedure by default — you must pair a Failure Conditional Formula with Fail On Step Error, or wrap the steps in a Try-Catch Block.
practices.specifics: Properties: 'Failure Conditional Formula' ("Specify a formula that evaluates to TRUE if the step has failed to execute successfully") and 'Fail On Step Error' (terminates the IP when that formula is true). HTTP actions write response headers (e.g. Content-Type), response status, and status code (e.g. 200) into an <ElementName>Info node — that node is what the failure formula reads. Try-Catch Blocks group steps so a failure is caught rather than propagated.
practices.why_it_matters: A failed HTTP action with no Failure Conditional Formula returns HTTP 500 payloads downstream as if they were data, and the IP reports success.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs assume IP steps behave like Apex — an exception aborts the transaction. They therefore omit Failure Conditional Formula entirely and produce IPs that swallow HTTP 4xx/5xx and carry on.

practices.practice: Check whether Data Mapper Versioning is enabled before editing any Data Mapper in production — it is off by default, which means editing a Data Mapper mutates the live one with no version to roll back to.
practices.specifics: Setup > Omnistudio Settings > 'Data Mapper Versioning'. Doc text: "By default, the Data Mapper Versioning setting is disabled." Contrast with OmniScripts, FlexCards and Integration Procedures, which are versioned and require deactivate/new-version to change.
practices.why_it_matters: OmniScript/FlexCard/IP habits (edit a draft version, activate when ready) do not transfer to Data Mappers. An 'edit' is a live production change with no undo.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs describe every OmniStudio artifact as versioned and tell the user to 'create a new version of the DataRaptor and activate it'. With Data Mapper Versioning disabled — the default — that workflow does not exist and the user has already overwritten production.

practices.practice: Reach for Turbo Extract only for flat, single-shape reads: it has no formulas and no mappings, and it breaks on single-quoted input field values.
practices.specifics: Data Mapper Turbo Extract supports input source, queries, output destination and options, but "it doesn't have formulas or mappings". Documented restriction: "Data Mapper Turbo Extract doesn't support multiple input fields with single quotation marks in the field values. Use a Data Mapper Extract instead." Load and Transform types deliberately have no queries because they do not retrieve from Salesforce objects.
practices.why_it_matters: Turbo is the correct performance answer for a plain record read, and the wrong answer the moment any field needs reshaping — teams pick it for speed and then bolt an Integration Procedure on top to do the formatting Turbo cannot do.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs recommend Turbo Extract as a drop-in faster Extract and then show a Turbo config containing formula rows and custom output JSON node mappings — neither of which Turbo supports. The single-quote input restriction is unknown to them entirely.
practices.verbatim_error_string: Data Mapper Turbo Extract doesn't support multiple input fields with single quotation marks in the field values. Use a Data Mapper Extract instead.

practices.practice: Keep a Data Mapper to three or fewer sObjects, filter and sort only on indexed fields, and never write a bare Equals-null filter — it silently fails to filter.
practices.specifics: Best practice: "keep the number of SObjects to three or fewer" per Data Mapper. Id and Name are always indexed. Documented defect/workaround: filtering with Equals (=) against a null value does not work; you must add a second condition using Not Equal To (!=). Example given: accountId = null AND phone != null. Use relationship notation instead of multiple extract steps when pulling parent data.
practices.why_it_matters: The null-filter failure is silent — the Data Mapper returns rows it should have excluded, and the OmniScript renders them as valid data.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: An LLM writing a Data Mapper filter for 'contacts with no account' emits a single accountId = null condition and calls it done. It also routinely designs 6–8 object Data Mappers because it maps the sObject graph rather than the ≤3 guidance.

practices.practice: Design OmniScripts against the published hard ceilings — 750 elements, 10 nested recursive block levels, 4 MB LWC — and treat ContextId as reserved.
practices.specifics: Maximum 750 elements per OmniScript. Maximum 10 levels of nested recursive blocks. LWC size limit 4 MB. Generated PDFs: 250 KB already generates slowly, 1 MB+ may time out. Do not assign ContextId inside an OmniScript — it is the reserved key for Record ID. Edit blocks in table mode are not screen-reader compatible; use FlexCards instead. Tables are not supported inside text blocks. Resuming a saved session with Edit Blocks can duplicate data unless you gate it with a conditional flag.
practices.why_it_matters: The 750-element ceiling and the 4 MB LWC ceiling are what force decomposition into reusable child OmniScripts; discovering them at element 740 means re-architecting a live process.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: Asked 'how big can an OmniScript get?', LLMs answer with vague advice about keeping scripts short for usability and never state 750 elements, 10 nesting levels, or 4 MB. They also write ContextId assignments in Set Values steps, which collides with the reserved Record ID key.

practices.practice: Plan FlexCard releases around single-active-version semantics: activating a version deactivates every other version, and an active FlexCard cannot be edited or deleted.
practices.specifics: "Omnistudio deactivates all other versions of the Flexcard" when you activate one. "You can't edit or delete an active Flexcard. To make changes, deactivate it first." New Version keeps name and author; Clone creates a separate FlexCard requiring full setup. After any FlexCard change, republish LWR Experience sites that use it or the change will not appear.
practices.why_it_matters: There is no side-by-side A/B of two FlexCard versions, and the LWR republish step is the reason 'I activated it and nothing changed' happens on community pages.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs propose running two FlexCard versions concurrently for a phased rollout, and they omit the LWR site republish entirely — so the guidance produces a change that appears in Lightning Experience but not in the Experience Cloud site.

practices.practice: When moving OmniProcess records between orgs with the CLI, strip isActive from the export query — an exported JSON carrying isActive=true fails the import.
practices.specifics: Export: sf data export tree --query "SELECT ... FROM OmniProcess WHERE OmniProcessType='Integration Procedure' AND id='<id>'" --target-org <alias> --plan --output-dir <dir>. Import: sf data import tree --plan ./<dir>/OmniProcess-OmniProcessElement-plan.json --target-org <alias>. Doc text: "Don't include isActive=true on OmniProcess when you export the Integration Procedure" and "If the exported JSON file has isActive=true, the import operation fails." Metadata/objects involved: OmniProcess + OmniProcessElement.
practices.why_it_matters: This is the number-one CLI migration failure for standard-runtime OmniStudio and the error gives no hint that the culprit is a single boolean in the exported JSON.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: An LLM writing an OmniStudio CI/CD script emits SELECT FIELDS(ALL) or an explicit field list that includes IsActive, because including it seems obviously correct for preserving state. The import then fails and the model's next suggestion is usually a permissions or record-type red herring.
practices.verbatim_error_string: If the exported JSON file has isActive=true, the import operation fails.

practices.practice: Move FlexCards via the OmniUiCard object, deploy their Data Mappers and Integration Procedures first, and re-apply custom CSS by hand — the CLI export does not carry it.
practices.specifics: Object: OmniUiCard. Export fields include OmniUiCardKey, OverrideKey, DataSourceConfig, SampleDataSourceResponse, ClonedFromOmniUiCardKey, VersionNumber, Namespace, Name, IsTrackingEnabled, PropertySetConfig, OmniUiCardType, StylingConfiguration, UniqueName. Plan file: OmniUiCard-plan.json. Constraints: you cannot import a FlexCard whose name+author combination already exists; global/custom CSS is not included in CLI exports and must be reapplied post-deployment; deploy related Data Mappers and Integration Procedures before importing FlexCards. When converting from managed package, activate the FlexCard and choose 'Deploy Standard Runtime Compatible LWC'.
practices.why_it_matters: The name+author uniqueness rule blocks the common 'copy prod card into a sandbox that already has it' step, and the missing CSS produces a card that deploys cleanly and looks broken.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs describe FlexCard migration as 'export the DataPack and import it', with no mention of OmniUiCard, the name+author collision, the dependency ordering, or that styling silently does not travel.

practices.practice: Do not plan a DataPack-based release process for standard-runtime OmniStudio: DataPack export/import from the standard designer is not supported, and OmniOut requires the managed package.
practices.specifics: Doc text: "Exporting and importing directly from the standard designer using data packs isn't supported; use Salesforce CLI instead." OmniOut is not supported without a managed package installation. Deployment model split: managed package runtime → DataPacks + Omnistudio Build Tool (formerly Vlocity Build Tool / VBT); standard runtime → Metadata API, sf CLI, or unlocked packages. The 'Omnistudio Metadata' setting in Setup > Omnistudio Settings must be enabled for Metadata API retrieve/deploy of Omnistudio standard objects; enabling it creates entries for existing components from the standard objects in the Omnistudio configuration tables.
practices.why_it_matters: A team that migrates to standard runtime while keeping a VBT/DataPack pipeline discovers their entire release automation is unsupported.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs answer every OmniStudio deployment question with 'use the Vlocity Build Tool and DataPacks', which is now both renamed (Omnistudio Build Tool) and wrong for standard runtime. They also never mention the 'Omnistudio Metadata' org setting, without which Metadata API deployment of standard objects does not work.
practices.gating_licence_or_permission: Setup > Omnistudio Settings > Omnistudio Metadata must be enabled for Metadata API deploy/retrieve of Omnistudio standard objects.
practices.verbatim_error_string: Exporting and importing directly from the standard designer using data packs isn't supported; use Salesforce CLI instead.

practices.practice: Split large OmniStudio exports: keep no more than 10 elements per data pack, or the export/import hits Apex heap or CPU limits.
practices.specifics: Doc guidance: "reduce the size of the data pack by unselecting dependencies during the export process... break the data pack into multiple smaller data packs. As a best practice, we recommend including no more than 10 elements in each data pack." Purpose stated: avoid Apex heap or CPU limit errors during export/import. Same 10-element guidance appears for FlexCard transfer.
practices.why_it_matters: Governor limits apply to the migration tooling itself, not just to runtime — an obvious-in-hindsight fact that turns a 'simple' release into an intermittent failure.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs treat OmniStudio migration as file copying and suggest exporting the whole project in one pass 'to keep dependencies intact'. The advice is exactly inverted: you unselect dependencies and shard to ≤10 elements.

practices.practice: Ignore two specific export-time errors from Integration Procedures that call BRE artifacts — they are documented as safe and do not indicate a broken export.
practices.specifics: Exporting an IP that calls a Decision Matrix: "You can ignore a Calculation Matrix: Not Found error when exporting an Integration Procedure that calls a Decision Matrix." Exporting an IP that invokes an Expression Set produces a "Calculation Procedure: Not Found" message that can likewise be safely ignored. Decision Matrix Action requires Input Parameters, Filter Value and Matrix Name; Remote Options support executionDateTime (sets the matrix Effective Date) and a Default Matrix Result for null returns. Expression Set Action Remote Options: includeInputs=true (folds inputs into output, used for pricing data) and reserialize=true (when the expression set does not produce expected results).
practices.why_it_matters: These two strings send release engineers hunting for a missing dependency that does not exist, and often trigger an unnecessary rollback of a good deployment.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: Shown 'Calculation Matrix: Not Found', an LLM diagnoses a missing or inactive Decision Matrix and tells the user to re-deploy it — the opposite of the documented answer, which is that the message is expected and harmless during export.
practices.verbatim_error_string: Calculation Matrix: Not Found

practices.practice: When exposing an Integration Procedure as an Agentforce action, be explicit about which version wins: an active user-created IP takes precedence over an active Salesforce-standard IP of the same name, in both Agentforce runtime and Flow.
practices.specifics: Doc text: "Agentforce prioritizes the user-created Integration Procedure during execution" when both a standard and a user-created version are active — this applies to Agentforce runtime and Salesforce Flow invocation. Editing an IP's input or output configuration automatically updates the related Apex classes, but Flow may temporarily cache an older version. Setup path: define input/output JSON, verify the data, add the Agent Action from the Asset Library in Agentforce Studio, configure agent/subagent, then activate the embedded IP.
practices.why_it_matters: An org that cloned a Salesforce standard IP to tweak it silently changes agent behaviour org-wide, and the Flow-side cache makes the change look non-deterministic.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs assume the Salesforce-provided standard IP always wins (the usual platform precedence for standard vs custom), and they do not warn that Flow caches the pre-change Apex signature after an input/output edit — producing 'it works in Agentforce but not in Flow' bug reports.

practices.practice: Use current product naming and do not describe OmniStudio as retired: as of Summer '26 it is actively developed, but several sub-products and names have moved.
practices.specifics: Current spelling in Salesforce docs is 'Omnistudio' (lowercase s). DataRaptor is now 'Omnistudio Data Mapper'. Vlocity Build Tool / VBT is now 'Omnistudio Build Tool'. Summer '26 items: Accelerate FlexCard Development with OmniStudio MCP (Beta); Invoke Autolaunched Flows in OmniStudio FlexCards (Pilot); FORMULA() arithmetic in SOQL WHERE clauses (Pilot); accessibility improvements auto-applied to FlexCards and OmniScripts. Retirements that are real: Document Generation 1.0 sunset 31 July 2025; Vlocity Public Sector managed package retires 1 May 2028. OmniStudio itself has no announced retirement — Salesforce published a Feb 2026 deployment roadmap (atomic deployment, automatic dependency mapping, cleaner diffs, 2GP packagability) targeted at H2.
practices.why_it_matters: Advice that names a retired tool or a retired product destroys trust instantly, and 'OmniStudio is being killed off in favour of Flow' is a widespread but unsourced community belief.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs repeat the Reddit-origin claim that OmniStudio is being merged into Flow or deprecated, and they consistently write 'DataRaptor' and 'Vlocity Build Tool' as current names. There is no official retirement notice for OmniStudio in Salesforce's Active Product & Feature Retirements list.

skills/omnistudio/integration-procedures uses chainableQueriesLimit: 50 and chainableCpuLimit: 2000 as its worked example. Those are legitimate conservative overrides, NOT the platform defaults — the documented defaults are 100 queries and 10,000 ms CPU (6 MB heap, 150 DML, 50,000 query rows, 20 SOSL). Nothing in the skill states which is which, so a reader can easily come away believing 50/2000 are the defaults. Recommend labelling them explicitly as overrides.

No factually fabricated error strings or inverted mechanisms were found in the OmniStudio domain during this pass. The bigger issue is absence rather than error: zero corpus hits for the Omnistudio permission set licence, the three standard-runtime FLS objects, OmniComponentErrorLog, ErrorLoggingEnabled, DefaultRequiredPermission, EnforceDMFLSAndDataEncryption, VlocityMetadata, or any Business Rules Engine numeric limit — i.e. the two markers the library measures as under-served (verbatim error strings, gating licences/permissions) are almost entirely missing from the thinnest domain.

areas.area: Service Cloud and Experience Cloud (case management, Omni-Channel routing, entitlements/milestones, Knowledge, Experience Cloud guest hardening + sharing, Service Cloud Voice)

practices.practice: Never write Database.merge()/merge() for Cases — the merge() call does not support Case at all. Lightning Case Merge is a separate UI/Aura feature, not the merge API.
practices.specifics: merge() supports exactly: "Lead, Contact, Account, Person Account, and Individual. You can only merge objects of the same type." Max "Up to three records can be merged in a single request, including the main record" and "Up to 200 merge requests can be made in a single SOAP call". External ID fields can't be used with merge(). Case is absent from the supported list.
practices.why_it_matters: An LLM-authored 'bulk case dedup' Apex job silently fails to compile or throws at runtime; teams then hand-roll a delete-and-reparent routine that loses EmailMessage/CaseComment history irrecoverably.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs confidently emit `Database.merge(masterCase, duplicateCase.Id);` or a SOAP merge() envelope with type="Case", because Case *does* have a MasterRecordId field and Lightning does have a Case Merge button — so the model pattern-matches to Lead/Contact/Account merge. The MasterRecordId field exists on Case only because the Lightning merge feature populates it; the merge() API never accepts Case.

practices.practice: Treat Lightning Case Merge as destructive by default: the non-master cases are DELETED unless CaseSettings.keepCaseMergeRecords is explicitly turned on. Set it before anyone merges in production.
practices.specifics: CaseSettings metadata field `keepCaseMergeRecords`: "When enabled, duplicate cases remain after merging rather than being deleted." Default is off, so merged (victim) cases go to the Recycle Bin. Case merge also fires `before delete` / `after delete` triggers on the losing records with MasterRecordId populated — there is no dedicated merge trigger event.
practices.why_it_matters: Support orgs merge hundreds of cases a week. If keepCaseMergeRecords is off, every merged case number vanishes from reporting and from any external system that referenced it, and after the Recycle Bin window the record is gone.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs state that merging cases 'closes the duplicates and marks them as merged' or 'sets Status = Merged', by analogy with Lead conversion. There is no Merged status — the victim cases are deleted, and whether they survive is a single org-wide metadata toggle the model never mentions.

practices.practice: Set CaseSettings.overEmailLimitAction and unauthorizedSenderAction deliberately — the default handling of over-limit and unauthorised inbound email is silent discard, which loses customer emails with no case, no bounce and no log.
practices.specifics: CaseSettings metadata: `overEmailLimitAction` accepts Bounce | Discard | Requeue — "specifying system behavior when daily limits are exceeded". `unauthorizedSenderAction` "Specifies what happens to email messages received from invalid senders" with options Bounce or Discard. `routingAddresses` carries per-address emailAddress, caseOwner, caseOrigin, casePriority.
practices.why_it_matters: On-Demand Email-to-Case rides Apex Email Services quota. Discard means an inbound support email produces no Case, no bounce to the customer, and no admin alert — the archetypal silent-failure mode. Requeue retries; Bounce at least tells the sender.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: Asked to 'harden Email-to-Case', an LLM produces attachment-size and threading advice and asserts over-limit email is 'queued and processed the next day'. It never names overEmailLimitAction or unauthorizedSenderAction, so the org ships with Discard and only discovers it when a customer says 'I emailed you three times'.

practices.practice: When debugging Email-to-Case threading, look at EmailMessage.ThreadIdentifier / ClientThreadIdentifier, not only the visible [ref:...:ref] string in the subject. Also budget for the EmailMessage 50-custom-field ceiling before adding integration fields.
practices.specifics: EmailMessage.ThreadIdentifier (API 56.0+): "A value used by third-party email clients to identify which thread an email belongs to." ClientThreadIdentifier serves the same purpose for the sending client. ParentId is "ID of the case that's associated with the email"; "RelatedtoId and ParentId should have the same value when ParentId is set." EmailMessage is capped at 50 custom fields.
practices.why_it_matters: Threading failures are the #1 Email-to-Case support ticket. Two distinct identifiers exist and a mail gateway can strip the human-visible ref token while the header-based identifier survives (or vice versa) — you cannot diagnose which without querying both fields.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs describe threading as purely the `ref:_00Dxxx._500xxx:ref` token in the subject line and tell you to re-add it to the email template. They do not know ThreadIdentifier exists as a queryable field (v56.0+), so their debugging recipe is 'inspect the email body' rather than 'SELECT Id, ThreadIdentifier, ParentId FROM EmailMessage'.

practices.practice: Do not assume an after-insert trigger, an after-save record-triggered Flow, or an immediately-following SOQL can see the owner that assignment rules chose — assignment rules run at step 9 of the order of execution, AFTER all after triggers.
practices.specifics: Order of execution, verbatim: step 9 "Executes assignment rules." step 10 "Executes auto-response rules." step 11 "Executes workflow rules." step 12 "Executes escalation rules." step 15 "Executes entitlement rules." All of these occur after the record is saved to the database (step 7) and after all after triggers execute (step 8).
practices.why_it_matters: Notification logic, Chatter posts and integration callouts that read OwnerId in after-insert get the pre-assignment owner (the running user or the default case owner), producing wrong-recipient alerts in production that never reproduce in a unit test using a single hardcoded owner.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs write an after-insert Case trigger that emails 'the assigned owner' and reason that assignment rules are 'part of the save', so the owner must be set. They also routinely place escalation rules before workflow rules. The correct sequence — assignment (9) → auto-response (10) → workflow (11) → escalation (12) → entitlement (15), all post-after-trigger — is one the model reconstructs from vibes.

practices.practice: AssignmentRuleHeader.assignmentRuleId can point at an INACTIVE assignment rule — use it to run a specific rule from an integration without disturbing the one active rule. Malformed IDs throw MALFORMED_ID.
practices.specifics: assignmentRuleId: "The ID of a specific assignment rule to run for the Case or Lead. The assignment rule can be active or inactive." You must specify either assignmentRuleId OR useDefaultRule, never both. The header also applies to Account, where useDefaultRule=true runs all territory assignment rules and false runs none. "Invalid ID formats (not 15 or 18 characters) trigger a MALFORMED_ID exception."
practices.why_it_matters: Orgs are hard-limited to one active assignment rule per object. The inactive-rule capability is the only supported way to run after-hours or channel-specific routing from an integration without toggling the org's single active rule.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs know DMLOptions.assignmentRuleHeader.useDefaultRule=true, but when asked for after-hours routing they propose a scheduled job that activates/deactivates rules, or a second active rule. They believe an inactive rule cannot be invoked, so they miss the one clean pattern the API explicitly supports.
practices.already_covered_by: skills/admin/assignment-rules (covers AssignmentRuleHeader + DMLOptions + one-active-rule); the inactive-rule-by-Id capability and MALFORMED_ID are not present
practices.verbatim_error_string: MALFORMED_ID

practices.practice: When escalation rules must run from Apex or an integration path, know that DuplicateRuleHeader.runAsCurrentUser is required for duplicate rules to respect sharing — by default Apex-invoked duplicate rules run in system context.
practices.specifics: DuplicateRuleHeader fields: `allowSave` — "when the Alert option is enabled, bypass alerts and save duplicate records by setting this property to true"; `includeRecordDetails` — true returns fields and values of the detected duplicates, false returns only record IDs; `runAsCurrentUser` — "Make sure that sharing rules for the current user are enforced when duplicate rules run". Available on create(), update(), upsert().
practices.why_it_matters: Without runAsCurrentUser, a duplicate rule executed from Apex can surface record IDs (and with includeRecordDetails, field values) for records the running user cannot see — an information-disclosure path that never appears in a sharing audit.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs set allowSave=true to 'make the insert work' and stop there. They do not mention that includeRecordDetails leaks duplicate field values, nor that runAsCurrentUser defaults to system context — so an LLM-written duplicate-check LWC returns records the community user was never allowed to see.
practices.already_covered_by: skills/apex/apex-record-clone-patterns, skills/data/data-quality-and-governance (allowSave present); runAsCurrentUser sharing-leak framing not present

practices.practice: Model case escalation timing with the exact EscalationRules metadata knobs: escalationStartTime (CaseCreation | CaseLastModified), businessHoursSource (None | Case | Static), and disableEscalationWhenModified — and remember Holiday records suspend both business hours and escalation.
practices.specifics: RuleEntry fields: `escalationStartTime` enum "CaseCreation" or "CaseLastModified"; `businessHoursSource` enum None | Case | Static; `businessHours` — "The hours when escalation actions are performed"; `disableEscalationWhenModified`. EscalationAction has `minutesToEscalation`, `assignedToType` (User | Queue), `notifyCaseOwner`, `notifyTo`, `notifyToTemplate`. BusinessHours: "Escalation rules are run only during these hours" and "If business hours are associated with any Holiday records, then business hours and escalation rules associated with business hours are suspended during the dates and times specified as holidays."
practices.why_it_matters: businessHoursSource=Case means the clock follows the Case's own BusinessHoursId, which can differ per case; businessHoursSource=None means the clock runs 24/7 through weekends. Getting this wrong produces a wave of 3am escalations or, worse, none at all on a public holiday when the SLA was contractually still running.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs describe the escalation clock as 'based on case age' and never mention that business hours can be sourced from the Case record itself (businessHoursSource=Case) versus a fixed schedule (Static) versus 24/7 (None). They also never mention that Holiday records silently pause escalation — so an org's Christmas SLA breach goes undetected.
practices.already_covered_by: skills/admin/escalation-rules covers CaseCreation vs Last Modified and one-active-rule in UI terms; businessHoursSource enum, disableEscalationWhenModified, and Holiday suspension of escalation are absent

practices.practice: Complete milestones by updating CaseMilestone.CompletionDate — CaseMilestone supports only update(). You cannot insert or delete a CaseMilestone, so 'create the milestone in Apex' is never the answer.
practices.specifics: CaseMilestone supported calls: describeLayout(), describeSObjects(), query(), retrieve(), update() — no create(), no delete(). CompletionDate is "The date and time the milestone was completed" and is the updatable field. IsCompleted, IsViolated and TargetDate are read-only/system-maintained; TimeRemainingInMins is a text field formatted "minutes and seconds", not a number, so it cannot be used in a numeric filter.
practices.why_it_matters: Milestone completion does not happen automatically when a case closes. The only supported completion mechanism is stamping CompletionDate, and any code that tries to insert a CaseMilestone to backfill SLA data fails outright.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs write `insert new CaseMilestone(CaseId=..., MilestoneTypeId=...)` to seed test data, and they filter reports on TimeRemainingInMins as if it were an Integer. Both fail. They also assume IsCompleted is settable — it is derived from CompletionDate.
practices.already_covered_by: skills/apex/entitlement-apex-hooks + skills/apex/case-trigger-patterns cover 'milestone does not complete on case close'; the update()-only API surface and the TimeRemainingInMins text-type trap are not stated

practices.practice: Use the exact MilestoneType recurrence API values when scripting or deploying entitlements: none | recursIndependently | recursChained — the UI labels ('Independent', 'Sequential') are not the metadata values.
practices.specifics: MilestoneType.RecurrenceType enum: `none` — "Specifies no recurrence for the milestone. The milestone occurs only one time until the entitlement process exits."; `recursIndependently` — independent recurrence; `recursChained` — sequential recurrence. Available API v29.0+. Related EntitlementSettings toggles: `enableEntitlementVersioning` (v28.0+), `enableMilestoneFeedItem` (v47.0+), `enableMilestoneStoppedTime` (surfaces Stopped Time and Actual Elapsed Time fields), `ignoreMilestoneBusinessHours` (shows time in actual hours rather than business hours).
practices.why_it_matters: A deployment with RecurrenceType 'Independent' fails validation. And ignoreMilestoneBusinessHours silently changes what every SLA report means org-wide — from business-hours elapsed to wall-clock elapsed.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs generate .milestoneType XML with human-readable labels ('Independent', 'Sequential', 'No Recurrence') because those are the Setup UI strings. They also never surface ignoreMilestoneBusinessHours, so an org that flips it to make dashboards 'simpler' unknowingly invalidates every historical SLA metric.
practices.already_covered_by: skills/admin/entitlements-and-milestones covers recurrence conceptually with UI labels; the metadata enum values and the EntitlementSettings toggles are absent

practices.practice: Account for the Entitlement record's own required BusinessHoursId when reasoning about which clock a milestone runs on — business hours exist at the Entitlement, entitlement process and milestone levels, not just the latter two.
practices.specifics: Entitlement object required fields include "Name, AssetId, BusinessHoursId, ContractLineItemId, and ServiceContractId". EntitlementProcess metadata has a `businessHours` field (API v30.0+) and each EntitlementProcessMilestoneItem has its own `businessHours` (v30.0+). CaseMilestone carries a BusinessHoursId reference. EntitlementProcess.entryStartDateField valid values include SlaStartDate, CreatedDate, ClosedDate, LastModifiedDate, StopStartDate. Case-level SLA state fields: SlaStartDate ("the time that the case entered an entitlement process" — updatable with Edit on cases), IsStopped, StopStartDate.
practices.why_it_matters: SlaStartDate is user-editable with only the Edit permission on Case, which means an agent can reset the SLA clock on a case. Any SLA-compliance report that does not account for that, or for the entitlement-level business hours, reports numbers the contract counterparty can dispute.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs present a two-level business-hours story (process, then milestone override) and say 'if neither is set, 24/7'. They omit that Entitlement.BusinessHoursId is a required field on the entitlement itself, and they never warn that SlaStartDate is editable by any user with Edit on Case — so their 'SLA integrity' checklist has no control for clock tampering.
practices.already_covered_by: skills/admin/entitlements-and-milestones states process-level and milestone-level only

practices.practice: In Omni-Channel routing metadata, skills-based routing is QueueRoutingConfig.isAttributeBased = true — it is NOT a routingModel value. routingModel only accepts LEAST_ACTIVE, MOST_AVAILABLE, EXTERNAL_ROUTING.
practices.specifics: QueueRoutingConfig: `routingModel` valid values are "LEAST_ACTIVE", "MOST_AVAILABLE", "EXTERNAL_ROUTING" (uppercase snake case). `isAttributeBased` — "Indicates whether this routing configuration is used with skills-based routing rules (true) or not (false)." `capacityWeight` = units consumed; `capacityPercentage` = percentage of agent capacity consumed; `pushTimeout` in seconds where "0 is returned when push timeout isn't enabled"; `routingPriority` is Required.
practices.why_it_matters: A generated .queueRoutingConfig with routingModel="Skills-Based" or "LeastActive" fails deployment. And picking capacityPercentage vs capacityWeight is a one-or-the-other modelling decision that determines whether a chat and a case can ever coexist on one agent.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs write 'set Routing Model = Skills-Based' — an option that does not exist in either the metadata enum or the routing-model picklist. They also produce camelCase enum values (LeastActive/MostAvailable) instead of the LEAST_ACTIVE/MOST_AVAILABLE the API requires.
practices.already_covered_by: skills/admin/omni-channel-routing-setup and skills/architect/omni-channel-capacity-model cover Least Active vs Most Available and capacityWeight; the exact enum casing, EXTERNAL_ROUTING, and isAttributeBased-vs-routingModel distinction are absent (and the routing-setup skill asserts a nonexistent 'Skills-Based' routing model)

practices.practice: Do not build Omni-Channel reporting or automation on triggers over UserServicePresence (unsupported) or on updating AgentWork (immutable). Read them; do not write them.
practices.specifics: UserServicePresence: "Apex triggers aren't supported with UserServicePresence"; delete is allowed in API v41.0+ and requires the Customize Application permission. AgentWork: "none of its fields can be updated" after creation, and records "can only be deleted if they have the status Closed, Declined, or Unavailable". AgentWork.Status picklist: Assigned, Canceled, Closed, Declined, DeclinedOnPushTimeout, Opened, Transferred, Unavailable. PushTimeout is in seconds; for inbound Voice calls (API v57.0+) values range 0–20 seconds.
practices.why_it_matters: Real-time supervisor dashboards and 'agent went idle' alerting are routinely specified as triggers on presence changes. That design cannot be built on-platform and has to be rebuilt on Platform Events or the Omni-Channel streaming API — discovered only after the trigger silently never fires.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs happily write `trigger UserServicePresenceTrigger on UserServicePresence (after update)` and an AgentWork field update to stamp a custom 'handle time' field. The first never fires; the second throws. They also omit DeclinedOnPushTimeout from Status handling, so decline-rate metrics under-count.
practices.already_covered_by: skills/data/omni-channel-reporting-data references AgentWork and UserServicePresence; the no-triggers and no-field-update constraints and the full Status enum are the depth to verify/add there
practices.gating_licence_or_permission: Delete on UserServicePresence requires the Customize Application permission (API v41.0+)

practices.practice: Set SkillRequirement.SkillLevel on the 0–99.99 scale and use IsAdditionalSkill + SkillPriority to make skills droppable, otherwise a skills-based work item can sit unrouted forever.
practices.specifics: SkillLevel: "The level of the skill required. Skill levels can range from zero to 99.99." IsAdditionalSkill: "After a designated timeout period, a skill marked as additional is dropped from Omni-Channel routing." SkillPriority is an integer "determining the order in which additional skills are dropped during routing if no agent possesses them." And: "When a work item requires multiple skills, it's routed to an agent who has all of the required skills."
practices.why_it_matters: Multi-skill requirements are ANDed. Without at least one IsAdditionalSkill=true escape valve, a work item requiring Spanish + Tier3 + Billing waits indefinitely if no single agent holds all three — a silent SLA breach with no error anywhere.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs set SkillLevel to 1–5 or 1–10 (a Likert scale they invent) and never mention IsAdditionalSkill/SkillPriority. Their skills-based routing design therefore requires an exact all-skills match with no degradation path — the single most common cause of 'work items stuck in the queue' in skills-based deployments.
practices.already_covered_by: skills/apex/omni-channel-custom-routing references SkillRequirement; the 0–99.99 range and the IsAdditionalSkill/SkillPriority drop mechanism are not present (99.99 only appears in FSL packages)

practices.practice: Query Knowledge with PublishStatus or Id in the WHERE clause, and never use bind variables against KnowledgeArticleVersion in Apex SOQL — use dynamic SOQL.
practices.specifics: "Article queries and searches in SOQL or SOSL require that you specify either the PublishStatus or the Id field in the WHERE clause." "You can't use binding variables in Apex SOQL statements with KnowledgeArticleVersion objects" — use dynamic SOQL instead. SOSL additionally requires Language in the WHERE clause and "You can search for only one publication status per article type in a single SOSL query." For archived articles, "also check that IsLatestVersion equals false in your WHERE clause." PublishStatus values: Draft, Online, Archived. In API v47.0+ the Language filter became optional for SOQL.
practices.why_it_matters: The bind-variable restriction defeats the standard parameterised-query pattern and pushes developers to string concatenation — which is exactly where SOQL injection enters a Knowledge search component exposed to guest users.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs write `[SELECT Id, Title FROM Knowledge__kav WHERE Title LIKE :searchTerm]` — which is invalid twice over (no PublishStatus/Id filter, and a bind variable on a Knowledge article version). When told to use dynamic SOQL they then concatenate the user input without String.escapeSingleQuotes, creating an injectable guest-facing search.
practices.already_covered_by: skills/lwc/knowledge-article-lwc and skills/apex/soql-object-limits-and-restrictions reference PublishStatus; the bind-variable prohibition (and its injection consequence) appears nowhere — grep for 'binding variable' + knowledge returned zero
practices.gating_licence_or_permission: Knowledge User feature license, plus View Articles; the Online PublishStatus requires the Manage Articles permission

practices.practice: Do not move Data Categories between orgs with the Metadata API — a DataCategoryGroup deploy is destructive by omission, and category developer names can never be changed.
practices.specifics: Deploying category changes "permanently removes categories and record categorizations that are not specified in your XML file"; when a category is deleted "Records associated with the deleted categories are re-associated with the parent category." A category's developer name: "The value for this field is defined once and cannot be changed later." Structural limits: "You can create up to 100 categories in a data category group and have up to 5 levels in a data category group hierarchy." Salesforce explicitly advises against Metadata API deployment of data categories between sandbox and production and recommends manual Setup creation.
practices.why_it_matters: A partial DataCategoryGroup in a change set silently wipes categories and re-parents every article's categorisation to the parent node. There is no undo — the per-article category assignments are gone and must be rebuilt by hand or by bulk load from a pre-deploy export.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs recommend 'add DataCategoryGroup to your package.xml and deploy it like any other metadata' and treat it as additive. Metadata deploys are usually additive; this one is declarative-replace. The model also treats data category developer names as renameable, so its 'taxonomy refactor' plan starts with renaming nodes.
practices.already_covered_by: skills/architect/knowledge-taxonomy-design covers the 100-category / 5-level limits and flattening strategy; the destructive-by-omission deploy behaviour, parent re-association, and immutable developer name are absent

practices.practice: Grant Experience Cloud guest users record access ONLY through guest user sharing rules (SharingGuestRule), which are read-only by design — external org-wide defaults are Private for guest and Public Read/Write is not an option.
practices.specifics: "For SharingGuestRule, the accessLevel field can be set only to Read." Available API v47.0+; booleanFilter and criteriaItems added in v48.0 (criteria-based); `includeHVUOwnedRecords` (required, v52.0+) "Controls whether high-volume community or site user-owned records are included". The resulting share rows are visible as CaseShare/AccountShare RowCause = GuestRule, alongside GuestParentImplicit — "The guest user has access because they have access to records related to the Account, such as opportunities, cases, contracts, or orders." Share access "must be set to an access level that is higher than the organization's default access level".
practices.why_it_matters: Guest-user over-exposure is the single most common Salesforce data-breach vector. Advice that says 'set OWD to Public Read Only so guests can see the records' exposes every record of that object to the anonymous internet and is the opposite of the platform's enforced model.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs (and, as of this scan, two files in this corpus) invert the mechanism: they say guests can only see records when external OWD is Public Read Only or Public Read/Write, and that guest sharing rules cannot reach Private-OWD records. That is the pre-Winter-'20 world. Today, guest external OWD is forced Private and the guest sharing rule IS the grant path — the existence of a read-only-capped SharingGuestRule type and the GuestRule RowCause only make sense if OWD is Private.
practices.already_covered_by: skills/security/guest-user-security and skills/admin/experience-cloud-guest-access both discuss guest sharing rules; the GuestRule/GuestParentImplicit RowCause values and includeHVUOwnedRecords are absent, and the OWD premise is inverted in guest-user-security (see stale_or_wrong_found)

practices.practice: Sharing Sets apply to far more license types than Customer Community — including Partner Community, Authenticated Website and the High Volume Customer Portal families — and their accessMappings can grant Edit, not only Read.
practices.specifics: SharingSet applies to: "Authenticated Website, Customer Community Login, Customer Community Plus, Partner Community, Customer Community User, High Volume Customer Portal, High Volume Portal, Overage Authenticated Website User, Overage High Volume Customer Portal User". Each accessMapping requires an access level (Read or Edit), a target object, the object field holding the lookup, and the user field it maps to. `profiles` — "The profiles of users that are granted access to the target objects" — must be on a compatible license. Description is capped at 255 characters. Since Spring '20 only users with View Setup and Configuration can access the object and only Manage Sharing can edit it; creating/updating sharing sets requires Customize Application.
practices.why_it_matters: Ruling Sharing Sets out for a Partner Community build pushes architects toward roles + criteria-based sharing rules or Apex managed sharing — orders of magnitude more expensive to build and maintain than an accessMapping, and it inflates the role hierarchy.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: The near-universal LLM answer is 'Sharing Sets are only for high-volume Customer Community (formerly High Volume Portal) users; Partner Community uses roles and sharing rules.' That was true years ago. The current supported-license list explicitly names Partner Community and Customer Community Plus. LLMs also assume Sharing Sets grant read only — accessMappings support Edit.
practices.already_covered_by: skills/security/experience-cloud-security discusses Sharing Sets but asserts a narrower license list (see stale_or_wrong_found); the accessMapping Edit level and the Manage Sharing / Customize Application gating are absent
practices.gating_licence_or_permission: Customize Application to create or update Sharing Sets; Manage Sharing to edit the object; View Setup and Configuration to see it (Spring '20+)

practices.practice: Use the real CommunitiesSettings API names when automating Experience Cloud org preferences, and know that enableGuestRecordReassignOrgPref was deprecated in v63.0 — its behaviour is now permanently enforced.
practices.specifics: CommunitiesSettings fields: `enableGuestRecordReassignOrgPref` — Deprecated as of API v63.0; `enableGuvSecurityOptOutPref` (v49.0+) — "guest user visibility can be turned off"; `enablePreventBadgeGuestAccess` (v53.0+) — "hides badges from guest users in Experience Builder sites"; `enableCspContactVisibilityPref` (v48.0+) — "allows users to see contacts from private accounts"; `enableCspNotesOnAccConPref`; `enablePowerCustomerCaseStatus` — "allows users with Customer Community Plus licenses to change case status"; `blockEmbeddedLoginUnknownURLRedirect` (v52.0+). Site-level Network metadata: `enableGuestChatter`, `enableGuestFileAccess` ("guest users view asset files shared with the site on publicly accessible pages and login pages"), `enableGuestMemberVisibility`, `enableMemberVisibility` ("the See other members of this site preference"), `selfRegistration`, `selfRegProfile`, `allowInternalUserLogin`.
practices.why_it_matters: enableCspContactVisibilityPref and enableGuestFileAccess are two of the least-understood exposure switches in Experience Cloud: one lets community users see contacts on private accounts, the other exposes asset files on public and login pages. Both are boolean org/site prefs that an unreviewed metadata deploy can flip.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs invent plausible-sounding preference names (enableGuestUserSecurity, secureGuestAccess, enableGuestRecordAccess) that do not exist in any metadata type. Deploying those fails; worse, when reviewing an org they check for settings that were never real and report a clean bill of health.
practices.already_covered_by: NONE — grep for enableGuvSecurityOptOutPref and enableGuestRecordReassignOrgPref returned zero hits across skills/

practices.practice: For Aura Experience Builder sites, ExperienceBundle metadata is inert until an admin enables it — Setup > Digital Experiences > Settings > ExperienceBundle Metadata API. LWR sites use it by default.
practices.specifics: "Only Experience Builder sites are supported, using the value ChatterNetworkPicasso." Aura-based sites: "Users must enable 'ExperienceBundle Metadata API' from Setup > Digital Experiences > Settings". "LWR sites use ExperienceBundle by default." Available API v46.0+; components use .json suffix in the `experiences` folder. URL path nuance: for authenticated LWR sites created before Winter '23 and for Aura sites, "the URL path prefix ends in /s," whereas newer LWR sites don't require that suffix. "The combination of definitionName + label must be unique in your org."
practices.why_it_matters: The /s prefix difference breaks every hardcoded deep link, email-template URL and redirect rule when a team migrates an Aura site to LWR — links silently 404 for authenticated users. And a CI pipeline that retrieves ExperienceBundle from an Aura sandbox without the toggle enabled returns empty and 'deploys successfully' with no site content.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs write an sfdx retrieve/deploy pipeline for ExperienceBundle with no mention of the org-level enablement toggle for Aura sites, and they treat site URLs as identical across templates — so their LWR migration plan has no link-rewrite step for the disappearing /s segment.
practices.already_covered_by: skills/devops/cicd-for-experience-cloud and skills/devops/experience-cloud-deployment-dev cover ExperienceBundle vs DigitalExperienceBundle ordering; the Aura enablement toggle and the /s URL-prefix divergence are absent
practices.gating_licence_or_permission: Setup > Digital Experiences > Settings > 'ExperienceBundle Metadata API' must be enabled for Aura sites

practices.practice: Automate Experience Cloud publish state via the Network object's Status field, whose API values do not match the UI labels: Live is labelled 'Published'.
practices.specifics: Network.Status picklist: `Live` — "The site is online and members can access it. Label is Published"; `DownForMaintenance` — site taken offline, setup access retained for admins; `UnderConstruction` — unpublished, accessible only to authorized builders. "This object is available only when your org has digital experiences enabled." Supported calls are describeSObjects(), query(), retrieve(), update() — you cannot create or delete a Network via the API. Related booleans: OptionsSelfRegistrationEnabled, OptionsAllowMembersToFlag, OptionsAllowInternalUserLogin, OptionsSendWelcomeEmail.
practices.why_it_matters: A release script that sets Status = 'Published' fails; one that sets 'Live' works. And because Network is update-only, site creation can never be fully scripted — that step stays manual or Metadata-API-driven.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs write `UPDATE Network SET Status='Published'` or 'Active', mirroring the Experience Workspaces UI. They also suggest creating sites via the Network object, which supports neither create() nor delete().

practices.practice: Assign Service Cloud Voice agents the Contact Center Agent / Contact Center Admin permission sets — those are the permission sets that gate editing VoiceCall records, and deleting call records requires Modify All Data.
practices.specifics: VoiceCall special access rules: "Only users with the Modify All Data permission can delete call records." To edit voice call records you need Sales Dialer (Dialer Outbound permission set) OR Service Cloud Voice (Contact Center Agent or Contact Center Admin permission sets). Key fields: CallDisposition (new / in-progress / completed), CallType (inbound, outbound, transfer, callback, consult, internal), CallQueuedDateTime, CallAcceptDateTime, CallRecordingId → VoiceCallRecording, ConversationId, RelatedRecordId (Account, Case, Contact, Lead, Opportunity).
practices.why_it_matters: 'Agents can't log call notes' is nearly always a missing Contact Center Agent permission set, not an Amazon Connect problem — teams burn days in the AWS console instead. And the Modify All Data requirement to delete VoiceCall means routine data-retention purges cannot be delegated to a support ops profile.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs name a 'Service Cloud Voice' permission set (which is how the add-on license is described, not how agent access is granted) and conflate Sales Dialer with Service Cloud Voice. They also never flag that VoiceCall deletion needs Modify All Data, so their data-retention design assumes a scheduled batch running as an integration user with ordinary CRUD.
practices.already_covered_by: skills/admin/service-cloud-voice-setup covers wizard setup and Live Media Streaming but names a 'Service Cloud Voice' permission set rather than Contact Center Agent / Contact Center Admin
practices.gating_licence_or_permission: Service Cloud Voice add-on license, plus the Contact Center Agent or Contact Center Admin permission set to edit VoiceCall; Modify All Data to delete VoiceCall; Dialer Outbound permission set for Sales Dialer

practices.practice: Choose the Omni-Channel capacity model at the ServiceChannel level (Status-Based vs Tab-Based) and, for status-based, name the StatusField — otherwise capacity is released the moment an agent closes a tab, not when the work is done.
practices.specifics: ServiceChannel.CapacityModel is Status-Based (work remains assigned until completion) or Tab-Based (capacity releases when the work tab closes). `StatusField` is "The picklist field that you use to track work status in the Status-Based capacity routing model". Other fields: `RelatedEntity` — "The type of object that's associated with this service channel. This field is unique within your organization."; `HasAutoAcceptEnabled`; `HasAfterConvoWorkTimer` (ACW for Messaging/Voice); `HasAcwExtensionEnabled` (v56.0+). Access rule: "Omni-Channel must be enabled", and since Spring '20 only authenticated internal and external users can access the object.
practices.why_it_matters: RelatedEntity being unique per org means you get exactly one service channel per object type — a hard architectural constraint that kills designs proposing separate 'Tier 1 Case' and 'Tier 2 Case' channels. Tab-based capacity plus an agent who closes tabs to tidy up produces silent over-assignment.
practices.llm_gets_this_wrong: LLMs design multiple service channels over the same object (one per work type) to get different capacity weights. RelatedEntity is unique per org, so this cannot be built — the correct lever is separate queues with separate QueueRoutingConfigs. They also omit StatusField, leaving status-based capacity non-functional.
practices.already_covered_by: skills/architect/omni-channel-capacity-model covers Tab-Based vs Status-Based mixing; the RelatedEntity org-uniqueness constraint and StatusField requirement are the depth to verify/add
practices.gating_licence_or_permission: Omni-Channel must be enabled

stale_or_wrong_found: INVERTED MECHANISM (high confidence, high severity) — skills/security/guest-user-security/SKILL.md:64 states "Guest users can only access records where OWD is Public Read Only or Public Read/Write" and references/llm-anti-patterns.md:33 states "Since Spring '21, guest sharing rules cannot grant access to Private OWD records. The only way to give guest users access to records is to set the OWD to Public Read Only." This is backwards and is the single most dangerous piece of guidance I found in this territory. Under Secure Guest User Record Access, external OWD for guest is Private and Public Read/Write is not available to guest at all; guest user sharing rules (SharingGuestRule) are the supported grant path, which is why the type exists, why its accessLevel "can be set only to Read", and why CaseShare/AccountShare expose a GuestRule RowCause (a share row is only meaningful above a restrictive OWD — the docs say share access "must be set to an access level that is higher than the organization's default access level"). Following this skill's advice literally means setting objects to Public Read Only to serve a public page, i.e. exposing every record of that object anonymously. The same package's templates/guest-user-security-template.md:43 repeats it ("Private OWD = zero guest access"), and references/well-architected.md:10 recommends "Public Read Only OWD with Apex filtering" as "the cleaner pattern". Note the corpus contradicts itself: skills/admin/experience-cloud-guest-access/SKILL.md:150 gives the correct instruction ("For Private OWD objects, create Guest User Sharing Rules that expose only the intended records"). Sources: meta_sharingrules.htm (SharingGuestRule), sforce_api_objects_caseshare.htm, sforce_api_objects_accountshare.htm.

TOO NARROW / WRONG LICENCE LIST — skills/security/experience-cloud-security/SKILL.md:61: "Sharing Sets are available for Customer Community and Customer Community Plus license types only." The SharingSet metadata doc lists Authenticated Website, Customer Community Login, Customer Community Plus, Partner Community, Customer Community User, High Volume Customer Portal, High Volume Portal, Overage Authenticated Website User, Overage High Volume Customer Portal User. The word "only" excludes Partner Community and the entire High Volume Portal / Authenticated Website family. The same file contradicts itself at line 156, where it lists "(Customer Community, Customer Community Plus, Partner Community)". Source: meta_sharingset.htm.

NONEXISTENT CONFIGURATION VALUE — skills/admin/omni-channel-routing-setup/SKILL.md:162 instructs "For skills-based routing: create Routing Configuration(s) with Routing Model = Skills-Based", and templates/omni-channel-routing-setup-template.md:32 offers "Least Active / Most Available / Skills-Based" as the Routing Model column. QueueRoutingConfig.routingModel has exactly three valid values — LEAST_ACTIVE, MOST_AVAILABLE, EXTERNAL_ROUTING. Skills-based is a separate boolean, isAttributeBased. A generated metadata file following this skill will fail deployment. Source: meta_queueroutingconfig.htm.

INTERNAL CONTRADICTION ON A NUMERIC LIMIT — skills/admin/knowledge-base-administration/SKILL.md:50 says "up to 5 Data Category Groups active for Knowledge", while skills/architect/knowledge-taxonomy-design/SKILL.md:56 and :66 say 3 active (maximum 5 created). Both cannot be right; the taxonomy-design figure (3 active of 5) matches the widely-documented limit. The DataCategoryGroup metadata doc I fetched confirms only the per-group limits (100 categories, 5 hierarchy levels) and explicitly does not state a group-count limit, so this needs adjudication against the Knowledge help doc before either number is trusted. Source: meta_datacategorygroup.htm.

LIKELY WRONG PERMISSION SET NAME — skills/admin/service-cloud-voice-setup/SKILL.md:96 says to "assign them the 'Service Cloud Voice' permission set". The VoiceCall object reference names the Service Cloud Voice permission sets as Contact Center Agent and Contact Center Admin (and Dialer Outbound for Sales Dialer). 'Service Cloud Voice' is the add-on licence name, not the agent permission set. Source: sforce_api_objects_voicecall.htm.

INCOMPLETE (not provably wrong) — skills/admin/entitlements-and-milestones/SKILL.md:93-96 presents business hours as a two-level model (entitlement process, milestone override) and concludes "If no business hours are attached (neither at process nor milestone level), the timer runs 24/7". BusinessHoursId is a REQUIRED field on the Entitlement object itself, and CaseMilestone carries its own BusinessHoursId, so at least three levels participate. I could not fetch the help topic that states the precedence order, so I am flagging this as needing verification rather than asserting the corpus is wrong. Source: sforce_api_objects_entitlement.htm, sforce_api_objects_casemilestone.htm.
